pending_commit.commit_message: tast.video.PlayVD: Add H.264, VP8 and VP9 play tests for the new VD's. This CL introduces additional tests for the new VD-based video decoder implementations. The tests play an H.264, VP8 and VP9 video respectively in the Chrome browser, and verify whether playback was successful. These tests are slightly different from the video.PlayDecodeAccelUsedVD tests, as they allow fallback to a software decoder, where the PlayDecodeAccelUsedVD tests only pass if HW acceleration was used. Introduce kernel.WilcoECTelemetry WilcoECTelemetry tests the Wilco EC's ability to respond to telemetry commands. The Wilco EC is able to return telemetry information (such as temperature and fan state) via sysfs: You write a binary command to the sysfs file, the kernel driver performs some filtering on the command to ensure it is sane, and the EC returns the binary result, to be read from the same file. You must keep the file descriptor open between the read and write for the response to be kept. This test checks for end-to-end communication with the EC, and checks that the driver performs some basic filtering and sanity checks. Since the responses are variable and opaque binary data, it's impractical to actually check the values of the responses. See https://chromium.git.corp.google.com/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/ea0f6a09a7a993fc7c781fd8ca675b29c42d4719/drivers/platform/chrome/wilco_ec/telemetry.c for the kernel driver. BUG=b:134407561 TEST=tast run ${DUT} kernel.WilcoTelemetry Change-Id: I3954b2e13acb538155996a7ec638724e7f2ecfad Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1747033 Tested-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

Speed up `get_dev_list` function The previous version ran `grep` three times for each device on the I2C and HID buses, which made it rather slow, sometimes taking as long as 100ms. Refactoring it to pipe all the device paths at once into a single `grep` call reduces the execution time to at most 10ms, normally around 5ms. (See [0] for more detailed timing data.) [0]: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1WBEcj-XEu4z823uW7n9mQnZfaimNWGLBt0Eu7GsLV1g/edit?usp=sharing BUG=none TEST=Ran on a Samus. Also ran the function on its own and manually verified the results, as well as running test data through the `grep` command to check cameras and Pixart devices were removed. shill: connection: Remove Binder Connection::Binder was previously used as a way of informing dependents when a Connection goes down. However, there is currently no code in Shill that actually needs this. The only Binder client is VPNService, but this usage is unnecessary. The lifetime of a Connection is controlled by Device, which will call SetConnection(nullptr) when removing an existing Connection, so VPNService can cleanly keep track of Connection removals without the use of Connection::Binder. Functionality will be added to VirtualDevice to map virtual devices onto physical devices. Doing this in Device rather than Connection allows for VirtualDevices to map to a physical Device even when the Device is not yet up (e.g. arc_wlan0 should still map to wlan0 even when we have not yet connected to a WiFiService). This also allows us to expose Device dependency information to the D-Bus interface (e.g. if we have both a cellular dongle and l2tp VPN, there is currently no clean way to determine which PPPDevice maps to which usage from the D-Bus interface). BUG=b:138464797 TEST=All unit tests are passing.
